_coordinate_verification: The earlier verification pass only checked bangalore.json against the GitHub repo (tannnmayy/et-ai) and the OpenAQ S3 archive files -- internal consistency between two things ultimately sourced from the same place, not independent confirmation. Fixed 2026-08-25: fetched https://explore.openaq.org/locations/{id} RAW HTML (not just its rendered text) for all 5 stations and found each page embeds a React Server Components data payload of the form 'coordinates:$R[N]={latitude:...,longitude:...}' tied directly to that location's own name field -- OpenAQ's own live platform database, independent of the GitHub repo and the archive CSVs. All 5 matched bangalore.json's committed coordinates EXACTLY (byte-for-byte on the decimal digits): 6983=(12.938539,77.5901) Hombegowda Nagar, 6984=(13.029152,77.585901) Hebbal, 6973=(12.920984,77.584908) Jayanagar 5th Block, 5548=(12.9135218,77.5950804) BTM Layout, 6975=(12.917348,77.622813) Silk Board. Additionally cross-checked 5548 (least corroborated: different ID range/network tag, has the real data gap and the CO unit bug) against an independent place-name source -- Wikipedia lists BTM Layout's locality centroid at 12.9250 N, 77.6086 E; the claimed station coordinates are ~1.95km from that centroid (flat-earth approx, same convention as ctm/grid.py), well within BTM Layout's actual extent (a multi-km-wide locality bordering Adugodi/Madiwala) and nowhere near an unrelated part of the city. Both methods confirm, neither contradicts.

_sensor_pair_distances_m._why_this_matters: ctm/assimilation.py's localisation_radius_m=10000 below is a HARD cutoff -- a pair separated beyond it gets ZERO direct assimilation correction at the other station regardless of whether the assimilation logic is correct (this is exactly what made the original 6983<->6984 spatial holdout structurally unable to show an effect: they're 10097m apart, just past the cutoff). All distances computed on the same flat-earth approximation ctm/grid.py's CTMGrid uses (111320 m/deg latitude, 111320*cos(lat) m/deg longitude).
_sensor_pair_distances_m._cluster_summary: 6983/6973/5548/6975 form a tight cluster, EVERY pair among them well under localisation_radius_m=10000 (max 4262m) -- a genuine spatial holdout is now possible within this cluster. 6984 remains isolated from all of them (>10000m to every other station) -- keep it as a held-out/contrast station, not part of an assimilation pair.

_phase16_calibration.method: Phase 16 -- calibrated on the disjoint 2019-07-17..2019-07-23 training sub-window (first 4 days), validated on that week's remaining ~3 days, never on the Phase 15 window. Full findings, including the two REJECTED changes below, are in PHASE16_CALIBRATION_REPORT.md -- read that before touching these numbers again.
_phase16_calibration.pm10_background_conc: NOT CHANGED. Trial value 48.304 (training-window mean) REJECTED and reverted to the original 35.0 -- real training-window pm10 (mean 49.1) was ~34% higher than real validation-window pm10 (mean 32.2), a genuine within-week drift (monsoon rain washout, not noise); the trial value overfit the wetter training days and made validation RMSE worse (22.6->23.7) and bias flip from -3.2 to +7.7 (over-prediction). See PHASE16_CALIBRATION_REPORT.md.
_phase16_calibration.pm25_background_conc: NOT CHANGED. Same rejection as pm10_background_conc -- trial value 19.124 REJECTED (real training mean 19.5 vs real validation mean 12.6, same drift); validation RMSE worsened 9.5->11.1, bias worsened +2.2->+6.3. See PHASE16_CALIBRATION_REPORT.md.
